hook: The Spanish adventurer who brought down the Aztec Empire.

pages.x: Hernán Cortés was born in 1485 in Medellín, in Spain, into a family of minor nobles. He gave up studying law and sailed to the Caribbean at 19, where he became a farmer and official, first on Hispaniola, then on Cuba.
In 1519 he sailed to Mexico with about 500 men, against the governor's orders. To stop anyone sailing home, he had his ships run aground and wrecked. Legend later said he burned them.

An enslaved Nahua woman, Malintzin, called Doña Marina by the Spanish, became his interpreter and adviser, and the mother of his son. Without her, Cortés could not have talked with Moctezuma or found his allies.

Many peoples hated Aztec rule. Cortés won over the Tlaxcalans and others, and tens of thousands of native warriors marched with the Spanish. He entered Tenochtitlan as a guest, and took Moctezuma prisoner.
pages.img: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire

pages.x: In 1520 the Aztecs rose up. Fleeing the city by night along a causeway, the Spaniards lost hundreds of men, many dragged down into the lake by the gold they carried. Cortés is said to have wept under a tree.

He came back with boats built in pieces and launched on the lake, and with his allies besieged the city for 75 days, while smallpox killed many of its people. On 13 August 1521 Tenochtitlan fell. On its ruins the Spanish built Mexico City.
Cortés destroyed the Aztec Empire and founded New Spain, the heart of Spain's empire in the Americas. To many Mexicans he is a symbol of conquest, and Mexico City has no statue of him.
pts: Won with native allies and the help of smallpox
